newsitem.title: INDIA: India budget seen boosting MNC food firms' profits.
newsitem.headline: India budget seen boosting MNC food firms' profits.

text.p: India's 1997/98 budget, running from April to March, will boost profitability and market share of multinational food companies in India, analysts said.
"They have dereserved ice-cream, biscuits and sugar confectionery, areas where MNCs (multinationals) can now expand," said an analyst at a European brokerage in Bombay.
The government had earlier reserved these industries for the small-scale, unorganised sector.

"This means Hindustan Lever can now enter the ice-cream business on its own," said an analyst, referring to a tie-up between Unilever Plc's Indian subsidiary with local ice cream maker Kwality Foods Ltd.
The dereservation will allow Cadbury India Ltd to enter the hardboiled sweet market, analysts said.
The hardboiled sweet market is now dominated by unlisted Indian firms such as Parle, Nutrine and Rawalgaon.
Britannia Industries Ltd, another food company, will also benefit by the dereservation, analysts said.
A reduction in corporate tax to 35 percent from 40 percent will boost the bottomlines of India's food MNCs as they are among the highest tax-paying firms, analysts said.
"This budget will push up MNCs' earnings," said Nikesh Shah, head of research at local broking firm N.H. Securities.

An excise duty cut in food products in this budget is expected to boost demand, especially from India's countryside, where branded foods have made deep inroads in recent years on the back of television advertising, analysts said.
"Dereservation, demand pull and profit push - overall this budget is very good for listed food companies," an analyst said.
Dabur India is one of the few listed Indian food companies to benefit from Friday's budget proposals, he said.
Indian industry bodies protested that the moves would adversely affect small-scale firms.

"This will bring sickness in the small-scale sector particularly in the dereserved sectors of small scale industries already in existence," Vijay Kalantri, president of the All-India Association of Industries, said in a statement.
